mainTopic: Proofs for who went up from בָּבֶל, the gravity of unfit marriages, and the story of רַב יְהוּדָה and רַב נַחְמָן
overview: The מִשְׁנָה lists the family-status groups that went up from בָּבֶל with עֶזְרָא, and the גְּמָרָא looks for a פָּסוּק behind each one. רַב חִסְדָּא shows from עֶזְרָא that גֵּרִים and freed slaves came along. A first proof that מַמְזֵרִים came, from טוֹבִיָּה הָעַמּוֹנִי, is knocked down by three challenges. It is replaced by a פָּסוּק in נְחֶמְיָה whose place-names (תֵּל מֶלַח, תֵּל חַרְשָׁא) hint at people of flawed lineage. The same פָּסוּק leads to teachings about how serious it is to marry a woman unfit in lineage, especially for money, and to the rule that whoever calls others unfit is unfit himself. A story follows: a man who habitually called people slaves insults רַב יְהוּדָה, who puts him in נִידּוּי and declares him a slave. The man summons רַב יְהוּדָה to רַב נַחְמָן's court. During the visit, רַב יְהוּדָה keeps correcting רַב נַחְמָן, about public labor, showy words, and a woman serving or being greeted. The amud ends in the middle of another teaching of שְׁמוּאֵל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the verse from the previous discussion
steps.stepSummary: The last words of a פָּסוּק that was quoted just before this point, as proof for the previous group in the מִשְׁנָה's list.
steps.simpleTranslation: "...she may not eat."
steps.whatsHappening: These two words finish a פָּסוּק that the גְּמָרָא quoted at the end of the previous discussion. That discussion is wrapping up here, and the next group in the list comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new argument. It is the tail end of a proof verse, ending with the idea that a certain woman may not eat. Once it is done, the גְּמָרָא moves on to the next group in the מִשְׁנָה.
steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous discussion. Do not try to connect it to גֵּרִים or מַמְזֵרִים, which come next.

phrases.english: she may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof verse from the previous discussion.
steps.raayaObject: The status of the previous group in the מִשְׁנָה's list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A פָּסוּק whose final words are 'לא תאכל'.

steps.title: Where do we learn that converts and freed slaves went up?
steps.stepSummary: The גְּמָרָא asks for a source that גֵּרִים and חֲרוּרִים were among those who went up from בָּבֶל.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Converts and freed slaves": from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא moves to the next group in the מִשְׁנָה's list and asks for a source. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מִשְׁנָה says גֵּרִים and חֲרוּרִים went up with עֶזְרָא. The גְּמָרָא wants a פָּסוּק that proves it, the same way it did for the earlier groups.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: "Converts and freed slaves": from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the מִשְׁנָה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פָּסוּק showing that גֵּרִים and freed slaves went up from בָּבֶל.

steps.title: רב חסדא's verse about those who separated from the nations
steps.stepSummary: רַב חִסְדָּא quotes the פָּסוּק in עֶזְרָא about people who separated themselves from the impurity of the nations and joined the returnees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רַב חִסְדָּא said: The פָּסוּק says, "And all who had separated themselves from the impurity of the nations of the land, to join them."
steps.whatsHappening: רַב חִסְדָּא answers with a פָּסוּק describing non-Jews who left the nations' ways and joined the returning Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People who 'separated from the impurity of the nations' are people who left עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה and became Jewish. That describes גֵּרִים and freed slaves. The פָּסוּק says they joined the returnees, so they were part of the group.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity of the nations of the land

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said,
for the verse says:
"And all who separated themselves from the impurity
of the nations of the land, to them."
phrases.notes: עזרא 6:21. 'To them' means they joined the Jews who came back from exile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פָּסוּק in עֶזְרָא describes people who left the nations and joined the returnees, meaning גֵּרִים and freed slaves.
steps.whatToRemember: גֵּרִים and freed slaves are those who 'separated from the impurity of the nations' (עֶזְרָא 6:21).

steps.title: Where do we learn that מַמְזֵרִים went up?
steps.stepSummary: The גְּמָרָא asks for a source that מַמְזֵרִים were among those who went up from בָּבֶל.
steps.simpleTranslation: מַמְזֵרִים: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא moves on to the next group in the list, the מַמְזֵרִים, and asks for a source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is harder than the last one. No פָּסוּק openly says 'מַמְזֵרִים went up,' so the גְּמָרָא will have to prove it indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: מַמְזֵרִים, children born from a forbidden union

phrases.english: Mamzerim: from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the מִשְׁנָה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that מַמְזֵרִים went up from בָּבֶל.

steps.title: טוֹבִיָּה הָעַמּוֹנִי married into Jewish families
steps.stepSummary: Two פְּסוּקִים in נְחֶמְיָה show that טוֹבִיָּה, called 'the servant' and 'the Ammonite,' married a Jewish woman, and that his son יְהוֹחָנָן also married a Jewish woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And סַנְבַלַּט the Horonite and טוֹבִיָּה the servant, the Ammonite, heard." And it is written: "For many in יְהוּדָה were bound by oath to him, because he was the son-in-law of שְׁכַנְיָה son of אָרַח, and his son יְהוֹחָנָן had married the daughter of מְשֻׁלָּם son of בֶּרֶכְיָה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא brings two פְּסוּקִים. The first tells us who טוֹבִיָּה was, and the second shows that he and his son married Jewish women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פָּסוּק calls טוֹבִיָּה both an 'עֶבֶד' (servant) and an עַמּוֹנִי (a non-Jew). The second פָּסוּק shows that he and his son married Jewish women. Children from these marriages could be מַמְזֵרִים, and the next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: People bound to him by oath

phrases.english: As it is written: "And Sanballat the Horonite heard,
and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite,"
phrases.notes: נחמיה 2:19

phrases.english: and it is written: "For many in Judah
were bound by oath to him,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חָתָן הוּא לִשְׁכַנְיָה בֶן אָרַח
phrases.english: because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah,
and his son Jehohanan had taken
the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah."
phrases.notes: נחמיה 6:18. So both טוֹבִיָּה and his son married Jewish women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That מַמְזֵרִים were among the returnees.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נְחֶמְיָה 2:19 and 6:18, about טוֹבִיָּה and his son marrying Jewish women.

steps.title: The view behind the proof: a נָכְרִי or עֶבֶד with a Jewish woman produces a מַמְזֵר
steps.stepSummary: The proof works because this תַּנָּא holds that a child born to a נָכְרִי or עֶבֶד and a Jewish woman is a מַמְזֵר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תַּנָּא holds that when a non-Jew or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a מַמְזֵר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא explains the hidden idea that makes the טוֹבִיָּה proof work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טוֹבִיָּה was a non-Jew and is called a servant. If a child born to a נָכְרִי or עֶבֶד and a Jewish woman is a מַמְזֵר, then his family's children were מַמְזֵרִים. This shows that מַמְזֵרִים were among the returnees.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole proof depends on one disputed ruling. That sets up the first challenge.

phrases.english: He holds that a gentile or a slave
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תַּנָּא of our מִשְׁנָה, who includes מַמְזֵרִים in the list.

phrases.english: who has relations with a Jewish woman:
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר נׇכְרִי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the פְּסוּקִים of step 5 prove there were מַמְזֵרִים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child of a נָכְרִי or עֶבֶד and a Jewish woman is a מַמְזֵר.

steps.title: What about the view that the child is כָּשֵׁר?
steps.stepSummary: The proof works only for the opinion that the child is a מַמְזֵר. What about the opinion that the child is כָּשֵׁר?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says the child is a מַמְזֵר. But according to the one who says the child is כָּשֵׁר, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא challenges the proof. Not everyone agrees that such a child is a מַמְזֵר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known disagreement about this child. According to the view that the child is כָּשֵׁר, טוֹבִיָּה's family had no מַמְזֵרִים, so the proof falls apart for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says
Valid, with no flaw in lineage

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says the child is a mamzer,
but according to the one who says the child is kosher,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling that step 6 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 6 that such a child is a מַמְזֵר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that the child is כָּשֵׁר, טוֹבִיָּה's descendants were not מַמְזֵרִים, so there is no source for the מִשְׁנָה.

steps.title: Maybe יְהוֹחָנָן had no children
steps.stepSummary: Even if such a child would be a מַמְזֵר, how do we know יְהוֹחָנָן had any children at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: how do we know he had children? Maybe he had no children!
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא adds a second challenge. The פָּסוּק says יְהוֹחָנָן married, but it never says he had children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A marriage alone does not create מַמְזֵרִים; only children do. Since the פָּסוּק mentions no children, the proof is missing a link.

phrases.english: And furthermore: from where do we know he had children?
phrases.notes: 'He' is יְהוֹחָנָן, טוֹבִיָּה's son, who married a Jewish woman.

phrases.english: Perhaps he did not have children!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate challenge to the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the marriage produced children.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פָּסוּק mentions only a marriage. Without children there are no מַמְזֵרִים.

steps.title: Maybe they were in אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל all along
steps.stepSummary: Even if there were children, how do we know they were in בָּבֶל and went up? Maybe they had been in אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל the whole time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: how do we know they were here in בָּבֶל and went up? Maybe they were there in אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל all along!
steps.whatsHappening: The גְּמָרָא adds a third challenge. Even if the children existed, nothing shows they came up from בָּבֶל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מִשְׁנָה is about who went up from בָּבֶל. If טוֹבִיָּה's family had always lived in אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, their children never went up, so they prove nothing about the returnees. With three open challenges, the proof for מַמְזֵרִים is now in serious doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: The טוֹבִיָּה proof for מַמְזֵרִים faces three challenges: (1) some hold the child is כָּשֵׁר; (2) maybe there were no children; (3) maybe the family never lived in בָּבֶל.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Here' means בָּבֶל, where the גְּמָרָא was written, and 'there' means אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל. Don't flip them.

phrases.aramaic: וְתוּ: מִמַּאי דְּהָכָא הֲווֹ לְהוּ וּסְלִיקוּ?
phrases.english: And furthermore: from where do we know they had them here and they went up?
phrases.notes: 'Here' is בָּבֶל.

phrases.english: Perhaps they were there!
phrases.notes: 'There' is אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, so maybe they never went into exile at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ מִמַּאי דְּהָכָא הֲווֹ לְהוּ וּסְלִיקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, separate challenge to the proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that טוֹבִיָּה's descendants came up from בָּבֶל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מִשְׁנָה is about who went up from בָּבֶל. A family that was always in אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל cannot prove that מַמְזֵרִים went up.

steps.title: A new proof from the פסוק in נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: After the טוביה proof was pushed away, the גמרא brings a different פסוק that lists people who went up from בבל and could not prove they were from ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof comes from here: "And these were they that went up from Tel Melach, Tel Charsha, Keruv, Addon, and Immer; but they could not tell their fathers' house and their seed, whether they were of Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the טוביה proof and brings a new פסוק as its proof. Next, it will explain what the strange names in this פסוק hint at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טוביה proof fell apart because of the problems raised in steps 7-9. This פסוק is better because it says outright that these people 'went up,' so it answers the step 9 question of whether they came from בבל. It also says that their lineage was in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (the old proof is dropped and a new one is brought)
Those who went up (to ארץ ישראל from בבל)
Their fathers' house, meaning their family line

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And these were they that went up from Tel Melach,
phrases.notes: נחמיה 7:61

phrases.english: Tel Charsha, Keruv, Addon, and Immer;
but they could not tell their fathers' house
and their seed, whether they were of Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the טוביה proof that steps 7-9 knocked down.
steps.raayaObject: That people of flawed lineage were among those who went up from בבל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחמיה 7:61, which lists people who went up and could not prove their family line.

steps.title: What תל מלח and תל חרשא hint at
steps.stepSummary: תל מלח hints at people who acted like סדום. תל חרשא hints at a child whose mother hushes him when he calls a man 'Father.'
steps.simpleTranslation: "תל מלח" means people whose deeds were like the deeds of סדום, which was turned into a mound of salt. "תל חרשא" means a child who calls out "Father!" and his mother silences him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the first two place-names are really hints about the people who went up. These hints show the proof: some of them were of flawed lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלח (salt) reminds us of סדום, which became salt, so it points to immoral behavior that produces ממזרים. חרשא sounds like 'silencing,' so it points to a child whose real father is uncertain. Both readings tell us that some of those who went up had doubtful lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: The city destroyed for its wickedness and turned into salt

phrases.english: "Tel Melach":
these are people whose deeds resemble
the deeds of Sodom, which was turned into a mound of salt.
"Tel Charsha":
this is one who calls out "Father!"
and his mother silences him.
phrases.notes: חרשא sounds like 'making silent.' She hushes him because the man he is calling 'Father' may not really be his father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק from step 10 actually proves the point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The names תל מלח and תל חרשא hint that people of doubtful or flawed lineage were among those who went up.

steps.title: The end of the פסוק refers to an אסופי
steps.stepSummary: The people who 'could not tell their fathers' house' are explained as an אסופי, a foundling picked up from the street.
steps.simpleTranslation: "But they could not tell their fathers' house and their seed, whether they were of Israel": this is an אסופי who was gathered up from the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the פסוק again and explains who it is talking about: a foundling whose parents are unknown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסופי does not know who his parents are, so he cannot even prove that he is Jewish. This is a different kind of doubtful lineage from the ones hinted at in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: A foundling, a child found abandoned whose parents are unknown

phrases.english: "But they could not tell their fathers' house
and their seed, whether they were of Israel":
this is a foundling
who was gathered up from the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הוּא אֲסוּפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱסַף מִן הַשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק, now its last phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people who could not prove they were from ישראל are foundlings with unknown parents.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: ישראל was meant to be like a כרוב but acted like a leopard
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads כרוב אדון ואמר as הקב״ה saying: I wanted ישראל to be precious like a כרוב, but they made themselves like a leopard.
steps.simpleTranslation: "כרוב אדון ואמר": רבי אבהו said: The Master said: I said that ישראל should be as precious before Me as a כרוב, but they made themselves like a leopard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו explains the last three names in the פסוק as a message from הקב״ה about ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדון is read as 'the Master,' meaning הקב״ה. אמר is read as נמר, a leopard, which stands for brazen behavior. In this first version the message is a complaint: ישראל was meant to be holy like a כרוב, but they acted boldly and badly.

keyTerms.meaning: A keruv, the angelic figure on the ארון, a symbol of being precious to הקב״ה

phrases.english: "Keruv, Addon, and Immer":
Rabbi Abahu said:
The Master said:
phrases.notes: אדון here means הקב״ה, the Master of the world.

phrases.english: I said that Israel should be before Me
as precious as a keruv,
but they made themselves like a leopard.
phrases.notes: The name אמר is being read as נמר, leopard. The two words sound alike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the proof to an aggadic reading of the remaining names in the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב״ה wanted ישראל to be precious like a כרוב, but they acted brazenly like a leopard.

steps.title: Second version: even as a leopard, ישראל stays precious
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבי אבהו says the message is a comfort: even though ישראל acted like a leopard, they are still as precious as a כרוב to הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבי אבהו said: The Master said: Even though they made themselves like a leopard, they are precious before Me like a כרוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי אבהו's teaching, which turns the message from a complaint into a comfort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions use the same three words. The difference is the order of the thought. In the first version, ישראל fell from being a כרוב to being a leopard. In the second, even as a leopard they are still loved like a כרוב.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק in נחמיה proves that people of flawed lineage went up from בבל. רבי אבהו also reads it as a message about how dear ישראל is to הקב״ה.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rabbi Abahu said: The Master said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׂמוּ עַצְמָם כְּנָמֵר –
phrases.english: even though they made themselves like a leopard,
they are precious before Me like a keruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the teaching in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when ישראל acts brazenly, they remain precious to הקב״ה.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: An unfitting marriage is like salting the whole world
steps.stepSummary: Anyone who marries a woman who is not fitting for him is considered by the פסוק as if he plowed the whole world and sowed it with salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: Anyone who marries a woman who is not fitting for him, the פסוק considers him as if he plowed the entire world and sowed it with salt, as it says: "And these were they that went up from Tel Melach, Tel Charsha."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה uses the same פסוק to teach how serious it is to marry a woman who is not fitting for him in lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads חרשא as 'plowing' and מלח as 'salt.' Sowing a field with salt ruins it so nothing can grow. So an unfitting marriage is pictured as damage to the whole world, because it brings children of flawed lineage into the nation.

keyTerms.meaning: Not fitting for him, here meaning not suitable in lineage
The פסוק considers him as if

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
Anyone who marries a woman
who is not fitting for him,
the verse considers him
as if he plowed the entire world
and sowed it with salt,
as it says: "And these were they that went up
from Tel Melach, Tel Charsha."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: כׇּל הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁאֵינָהּ הוֹגֶנֶת לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 10 to teach a lesson about marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying a woman unfit in lineage is treated as if one plowed the whole world and sowed it with salt.

steps.title: רב: Marrying for money brings improper children
steps.stepSummary: Anyone who marries a woman only for her money will have children who are not proper, as the פסוק in הושע says.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב אדא said in the name of רב: Anyone who marries a woman for the sake of money will have children who are not proper, as it says: "They betrayed ה׳, for they bore strange children."
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds a related teaching: marrying a woman only because of her money leads to children who do not turn out well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of step 15. There the problem was an unfitting match. Here the problem is the wrong motive, money, which leads a man to overlook her lineage. The פסוק in הושע links betraying ה׳ with 'strange children.'
steps.whatToRemember: The same פסוק that proves flawed lineages went up from בבל also teaches how harmful it is to marry someone unfit, especially for money.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Adda said in the name of Rav:
Anyone who marries a woman for the sake of money
will have children who are not proper,
as it says: "They betrayed the Lord,
phrases.notes: הושע 5:7

phrases.english: for they bore strange children."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה לְשׁוּם מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related warning about marrying for the wrong reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Marrying a woman for money leads to children who are not proper.

steps.title: The money from a money-marriage will not last
steps.stepSummary: The reading of the פסוק continues: the money will be lost, both his share and hers, and quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think at least the money stays. So the פסוק says: 'Now the month will eat them up with their portions.' You might think only his portion is lost and not hers. So the פסוק says 'their portions.' You might think it takes a long time. So the פסוק says 'month.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the פסוק from הושע about someone who marries for money. It uses three words of the פסוק to answer three possible thoughts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'you might think' (שמא תאמר) is answered by a word in the פסוק. 'Portions' shows the money is lost. The plural shows the wife's share is lost too. 'Month' shows it happens fast. The punishment matches the sin: he married for money, so the money is what he loses.

keyTerms.meaning: And perhaps you will say (a possible mistaken thought)
The money escapes (is spared from the punishment)

phrases.english: And perhaps you will say the money is spared,
the verse teaches:
"Now the month shall devour them with their portions."
phrases.notes: הושע 5:7

phrases.english: And perhaps you will say: his portion, but not her portion,
the verse teaches: "their portions."
And perhaps you will say it happens after a long time,
the verse teaches: "month."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the reading of the פסוק in הושע from Step 16 about marrying for money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who marries for money loses the money, both his share and his wife's, and quickly.

steps.title: How does 'month' show it happens fast?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the word 'month' teaches that the money is lost quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we see this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask how the word 'month' proves that the loss comes quickly. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A month could just be a time marker, so it is not obvious it means 'fast.' The גמרא wants the exact way the word teaches speed.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this implied? Where do we see it?

phrases.english: What is the implication?
phrases.notes: He is asking how the word 'month' from the last step shows the money disappears fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the last derivation, the word 'month'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word חודש shows that the money is lost quickly.

steps.title: A month comes, a month goes, and the money is gone
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains: within the passing of one month, their money is already lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: A month comes in, a month goes out, and their money is lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question. 'Month' means the money is gone within a single month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the month itself 'eats' them. So by the time one month starts and ends, the money is gone. This finishes the point that marrying for money brings a fast loss of that very money.
steps.whatToRemember: Marrying for money backfires: the money (his and hers) is lost, and quickly, within a month.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
A month comes in and a month goes out
and their money is lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Within one month the money is already gone.

steps.title: אליהו ties him and הקב״ה whips him
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says that whoever marries an unsuitable woman is tied up by אליהו and whipped by הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב אדא said, and some say רבי סלא said in the name of רב המנונא: Anyone who marries a woman who is not fitting for him, אליהו ties him up and הקב״ה straps him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement describes the punishment for marrying a woman who is not fitting for a man because of her lineage. It is pictured like a person getting lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 compared this marriage to sowing the world with salt. Now the picture is of מלקות: אליהו ties the man down like a person about to be whipped, and הקב״ה gives the lashes. It shows how seriously Heaven takes a bad match.

keyTerms.meaning: Straps him, whips him with a strap

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Rav Adda said,
and some say Rabbi Salla said
that Rav Hamnuna said:
Anyone who marries a woman
who is not fitting for him,
Elijah ties him up
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, straps him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב אַדָּא וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי סַלָּא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the theme of Step 15 (an unsuitable wife) with a new statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who marries an unsuitable woman is punished by Heaven, pictured as lashes from אליהו and הקב״ה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: אליהו writes and הקב״ה signs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא backs up and widens רב המנונא's statement: woe to one who damages his children's and family's lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: About all of them, אליהו writes and הקב״ה signs: Woe to the one who makes his children unfit, and who damages his family, and who marries a woman not fitting for him. אליהו ties him up and הקב״ה straps him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב המנונא, with more details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא pictures a court document: אליהו writes it and הקב״ה signs it. It lists three linked wrongs: making his children unfit, damaging his family line, and marrying an unsuitable woman. Then it ends with the same words as רב המנונא, so it supports his statement.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught (introduces a ברייתא)
One who makes his children unfit
One who damages his family's lineage

phrases.english: And it was taught: About all of them,
Elijah writes
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, signs:
Woe to the one who makes his children unfit,
and to the one who damages his family,
and to the one who marries a woman not fitting for him;
Elijah ties him up
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, straps him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports and expands רב המנונא's statement from Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's statement that אליהו ties and הקב״ה straps the one who marries an unsuitable woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same ending words, adding the written-and-signed picture.

steps.title: Whoever calls others unfit is unfit himself
steps.stepSummary: One who keeps calling others unfit is himself unfit and never praises anyone; שמואל says he accuses others of his own flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whoever calls others unfit is himself unfit. And he never says anything in praise of others. And שמואל said: He calls others unfit with his own flaw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a sign for spotting a person with a lineage problem: he is always calling others unfit and never praises anyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line says the habit of criticizing others' lineage shows the critic's own lineage is flawed. שמואל adds that the exact flaw he accuses others of is the one he himself has. This sets up the story that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever calls others unfit is himself unfit
He accuses others with his own flaw

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a בית דין ruling someone unfit. It is about a person who has a habit of insulting other people's lineage.

phrases.english: And whoever calls others unfit is himself unfit.
And he never speaks in praise of others,
and Shmuel said: He disqualifies others with his own flaw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishment for damaging lineage to a sign for recognizing a flawed lineage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who habitually calls others unfit is himself unfit, and his accusation reveals his own flaw.

steps.title: The man from נהרדעא insults רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A man in a butcher shop in פומבדיתא is told to wait for רב יהודה's servant, insults רב יהודה, and is put in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man from נהרדעא went into a butcher shop in פומבדיתא. He said: Give me meat. They said: Wait until the servant of רב יהודה בר יחזקאל takes his, and then we will give you. He said: Who is this יהודה בר שויסקאל that he should go before me and take before me?! They went and told רב יהודה, and he put him in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will show the rule of the last step in action. Here the man insults רב יהודה and gets put in נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man mocks רב יהודה by twisting his father's name יחזקאל into an insulting name. Insulting a תלמיד חכם brings נידוי, so רב יהודה puts him in נידוי. The story is not finished yet; the next step ties it to שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A mocking twist of the name יחזקאל
He put him in נידוי (excommunicated him)

phrases.english: There was a certain man from Neharde'a
who went into a butcher shop in Pumbedita.
He said to them: Give me meat.
They said to him: Wait

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּשָׁקֵיל (לְ)שַׁמָּעֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
phrases.english: until the servant of Rav Yehuda bar Yeḥezkel takes his,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter in round brackets, so read it simply as 'the servant of רב יהודה takes.'

phrases.english: and then we will give to you.
He said: Who is Yehuda bar Sheviske'el,
phrases.notes: He is mocking רב יהודה by twisting his father's name יחזקאל into an insult about loving meat.

phrases.english: that he should go ahead of me, that he should take before me?!
They went and told Rav Yehuda.
He excommunicated him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּמִנְּהַרְדְּעָא דְּעָל לְבֵי מַטְבְּחַיָּא בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story that will illustrate the rule of Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Insulting a תלמיד חכם leads to נידוי.

steps.title: He calls people slaves, so רב יהודה declares him a slave
steps.stepSummary: They tell רב יהודה the man often calls people slaves, and רב יהודה announces that he himself is a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: He is used to calling people 'slaves.' רב יהודה announced about him that he is a slave.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by applying שמואל's rule. The man who always calls others slaves is declared a slave himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly שמואל's 'במומו פוסל': the flaw he accuses others of is his own flaw. So רב יהודה publicly announces that the man is a slave, which affects whom he may marry.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to, in the habit of

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule in action: a man who habitually calls others 'slaves' shows that he himself is a slave.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule 'במומו פוסל' was used for a real public announcement about a person's lineage, not only as a moral lesson.

phrases.english: They said: He is in the habit of calling people "slaves."
He announced about him that he is a slave.
phrases.notes: רב יהודה is using שמואל's rule from Step 22: he calls others what he himself is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and connects it to שמואל's rule in Step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Based on במומו פוסל, the man who calls others slaves is publicly declared a slave.

steps.title: The insulted man summons רב יהודה to court
steps.stepSummary: The man from the butcher shop summons רב יהודה to be judged before רב נחמן, and the summons arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: That man went and summoned רב יהודה to judgment before רב נחמן. The summons note arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the man who was put in נידוי strikes back by calling רב יהודה to court before רב נחמן. This sets up the visit that fills the rest of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man claims רב יהודה wrongly put him in נידוי, so he takes him to a different judge. That creates the question in the next step: does רב יהודה have to answer the summons?

keyTerms.meaning: He summoned him to a court case

phrases.english: That man went and summoned him to judgment
phrases.notes: "That man" is the one from the butcher shop whom רב יהודה put in נידוי.

phrases.english: before רב נחמן.
The summons note arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the man put in נידוי by רב יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man summons רב יהודה to רב נחמן's court.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks רב הונא whether to go
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה goes to רב הונא and asks if he must answer the summons.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה went to רב הונא and asked: Should I go or not go?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה is unsure if he has to show up, so he asks רב הונא for advice. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about whether a great scholar is bound by another court's summons. It is a real practical question, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Should I go or not go?

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל רַב יְהוּדָה לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: רב יהודה went before רב הונא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵיזִיל אוֹ לָא אֵיזִיל?
phrases.english: He said to him: Should I go or should I not go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the summons that just arrived.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב יהודה obligated to answer רב נחמן's summons?

steps.title: רב הונא: not required, but go out of respect
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says a great man like רב יהודה need not go, but he should go to honor the house of the ראש גלותא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: As for being obligated, you don't need to go, since you are a great man. But because of the honor of the house of the נשיא, get up and go.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers: by law you don't have to go, but go anyway out of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels here: strict obligation and respect. רב יהודה's greatness frees him from the obligation, but honoring the house of the ראש גלותא is reason enough to go.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor of the house of the נשיא (the ראש גלותא)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵיזָל לָא מִיבְּעֵי לָךְ לְמֵיזַל,
phrases.english: He said to him: As for going, you are not required to go,
since you are a great man,
but because of the honor of the house of the נשיא,
phrases.notes: רב נחמן was connected by marriage to the family of the ראש גלותא, so ignoring him would slight that family.

phrases.english: get up and go.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No legal obligation, but go out of respect for the house of the ראש גלותא.

steps.title: רב יהודה challenges רב נחמן for building in public
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה finds רב נחמן building a railing and asks: doesn't a community leader have to avoid manual labor in front of three people?
steps.simpleTranslation: He arrived and found him building a railing. He said: Doesn't the master hold like רב הונא בר אידי said in the name of שמואל: once a man is appointed leader over the community, he may not do labor in front of three people?
steps.whatsHappening: As soon as he arrives, רב יהודה challenges רב נחמן's behavior using a rule from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule protects the dignity of a communal leader: he should not be seen doing manual work before three people. רב נחמן is a leader and is building in public, so it looks like he is breaking that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A leader appointed over the community
In front of three people (in public)

phrases.english: He came and found him making a railing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר
phrases.english: He said to him: Doesn't the master hold

phrases.aramaic: לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר אִידִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: by that which רב הונא בר אידי said in the name of שמואל:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּתְמַנָּה אָדָם פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּבּוּר
phrases.english: once a person has been appointed leader over the community,
he is forbidden to do labor in front of three people?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר אִידִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once רב יהודה follows the advice and arrives, the meeting opens with a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's building a railing in public
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל forbids a communal leader from doing labor before three; רב נחמן is doing just that.

steps.title: רב נחמן: it's just a small fence
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that he is only making a little גונדריתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: It's just a small bit of fence that I'm making.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself by downplaying the work: it's only a small piece of fencing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He suggests the job is too minor to count as the kind of labor שמואל meant. Notice he uses an unusual word, גונדריתא, which sets up רב יהודה's next comment.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is a small bit of fence
that I am making.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about public labor.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Building a railing in public is forbidden labor for a leader.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only a tiny fence, not real labor.

steps.title: רב יהודה criticizes the word גונדריתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks why רב נחמן didn't use the Torah's word מעקה or the חכמים's word מחיצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Is the word מעקה written in the Torah, or מחיצה that the רבנן said, so hateful to you?
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of arguing about the labor, רב יהודה now attacks the fancy word רב נחמן used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's point is that a person should speak either the Torah's language or the חכמים's language, not an unusual showy word. This starts a pattern that repeats in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition (the word the חכמים use)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סְנֵיא ״מַעֲקֶה״ דִּכְתִיב בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: Is "railing," which is written in the Torah, distasteful to you,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:8

phrases.english: or "partition," which the Sages said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks on the word used in רב נחמן's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are perfectly good words from the Torah and the חכמים; why use an odd one?

steps.title: Criticizing the word קרפיטא for bench
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן invites him to sit on a קרפיטא, and רב יהודה asks why not say ספסל or איצטבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Let the master sit on the bench (קרפיטא). He said: Is ספסל, which the רבנן said, or איצטבא, which people say, hateful to you?
steps.whatsHappening: The same pattern repeats: רב נחמן uses a fancy word, and רב יהודה corrects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the two good options are the חכמים's word and the everyday word people use. Either is fine; only the showy word is the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual word for a bench

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master sit on the bench.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וּמִי סְנֵי ״סַפְסָל״ דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: He said to him: Is "bench" (ספסל), which the Sages said, distasteful to you,
or "bench" (איצטבא), which people say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second round of the word-correction pattern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Use the חכמים's word or the common word, not a showy one.

steps.title: Saying אתרונגא is a third of arrogance
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן offers him an אתרונגא, and רב יהודה quotes שמואל that this word shows a third of haughtiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Let the master eat a citron (אתרונגא). He said: So said שמואל: whoever says אתרונגא has a third of arrogance. Either say אתרוג like the רבנן call it, or אתרוגא like people say.
steps.whatsHappening: The pattern repeats a third time, but now רב יהודה backs it up with a saying of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל calls the fancy word a sign of a bit of arrogance, because it shows off. This explains the reason behind all of רב יהודה's corrections: showy speech reflects pride.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master eat a citron.
He said to him: This is what שמואל said:
Anyone who says "etronga"
has a third of haughtiness of spirit.
Either say "etrog," as the Sages called it,
or "etroga," as people say.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר ״אֶתְרוּנְגָּא״ תִּילְתָּא בְּרָמוּת רוּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third round of the pattern, now with a source from שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל says this word shows arrogance; use the חכמים's or the common word.

steps.title: Criticizing the word אנבגא for a cup
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן offers a drink from an אנבגא, and רב יהודה asks why not say איספרגוס or אנפק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Let the master drink a cup (אנבגא). He said: Is איספרגוס, as the רבנן call it, or אנפק, as people say, hateful to you?
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth round: another fancy word from רב נחמן, another correction from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again two acceptable choices are given, the חכמים's word and the people's word. רב יהודה is consistent: every showy word gets corrected.

keyTerms.meaning: A fancy word for a drinking cup
A drink/cup term the חכמים use

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master drink a cup.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סְנֵי ״אִיסְפָּרָגוֹס״ דְּקַרְיוּהּ רַבָּנַן
phrases.english: He said to him: Is "ispargus," as the Sages called it, distasteful to you,
or "anpak," as people say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth and last round of the word-correction pattern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Use the חכמים's or the common word instead of a showy one.

steps.title: Objection to having דונג serve drinks
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks his daughter דונג to pour, and רב יהודה quotes שמואל: one may not be served by a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Let דונג come and pour for us. He said: So said שמואל: one may not make use of a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב יהודה objects to something else: having a woman serve them, based on שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts from words to conduct. שמואל's rule says a man should not use a woman to serve him, and רב יהודה applies it here.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not be served by a woman

phrases.english: He said to him: Let דונג come and pour for us.
phrases.notes: דונג is רב נחמן's daughter.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what שמואל said:
One may not make use of a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁים בְּאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from correcting words to challenging conduct.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל forbids being served by a woman.

steps.title: רב נחמן: she is a minor
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that דונג is a קטנה, so the rule shouldn't apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends himself: his daughter is still a young girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He assumes שמואל's rule is only about adult women. If so, a קטנה would be allowed to serve.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who is a minor

phrases.english: She is a minor.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves it unsaid, but this is רב נחמן answering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection about being served by a woman.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any woman, even a girl, is included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only covers adult women, and דונג is a קטנה.

steps.title: שמואל said explicitly: no woman at all
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rejects the answer: שמואל said clearly that it applies to any woman, adult or minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said explicitly: one may not make use of a woman at all, whether adult or minor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה shuts down רב נחמן's defense by quoting שמואל's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן tried to limit the rule to adults. רב יהודה shows שמואל already ruled out that distinction, so a קטנה is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether an adult or a minor

steps.whatToRemember: In this meeting רב יהודה keeps correcting רב נחמן: public labor, showy words, and being served by a woman. The last point is settled clearly: שמואל's rule includes even a young girl.

phrases.english: שמואל said explicitly:
phrases.notes: This is רב יהודה's reply to רב נחמן.

phrases.english: One may not make use of a woman at all,
whether an adult or a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer that she is a minor.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the distinction between adult and minor
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל explicitly included minors in the rule.

steps.title: Send greetings to ילתא? A woman's voice is ערוה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן invites רב יהודה to send greetings to his wife ילתא. רב יהודה objects by quoting שמואל: a woman's voice is ערוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Master send greetings of peace to ילתא. He said to him: This is what שמואל said: A woman's voice is ערוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן makes another friendly suggestion, and רב יהודה again pushes back with a teaching from שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the earlier steps: רב נחמן offers a polite gesture and רב יהודה finds a problem with it. This time the problem is not about wording. It is a halachic rule: speaking with a woman, even only to greet her, involves hearing her voice, which שמואל calls ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a polite way of saying 'you'
A woman's voice is considered ערוה (immodesty)

phrases.english: Let the Master send greetings of peace to Yalta.
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן speaking. ילתא is his wife.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:
A woman's voice is nakedness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the exchange about דונג pouring, רב נחמן makes a new suggestion, and רב יהודה rejects it with another teaching of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's suggestion to send greetings to ילתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Greeting a woman means talking with her and hearing her voice, and שמואל says קול באשה ערוה.

steps.title: Send the greeting through a messenger
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the greeting can be sent through a שליח, so רב יהודה will not hear her voice directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible through a messenger.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tries to get around רב יהודה's objection: let a שליח carry the greeting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection was about hearing a woman's voice. If a שליח delivers the greeting, רב יהודה never speaks with ילתא himself, so the problem of קול באשה ערוה seems to go away.

phrases.english: It is possible through a messenger.
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן again. He means the greeting can be sent so that רב יהודה never speaks to her himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 37 by changing how the greeting is delivered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Workaround: change the method so the rule no longer applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Greeting ילתא means speaking with her directly, so it is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The greeting can go through a שליח, so no voice is heard directly.

steps.title: רב יהודה starts to quote שמואל again
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה begins to reject the messenger idea by quoting שמואל once more. The quote itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line opens רב יהודה's rejection of the שליח idea. The גמרא is setting up the next move: the actual teaching of שמואל comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have the opening formula. The words 'this is what שמואל said' tell us that רב יהודה will not accept the workaround either, and that he will bring another teaching of שמואל against it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the rest of the sentence here. The words of שמואל continue on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to challenge the שליח answer of step 38.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to send greetings through a שליח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Will be explained by the teaching of שמואל that continues on the next amud.
